claims.text: The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
As-received HfZrTiTa0.53 exhibits limited strain hardening under high-strain-rate adiabatic deformation.
As-received HfZrTiTa0.53 exhibits poor uniform deformation and rapid failure at high strain rates under adiabatic conditions.
Warm rolling followed by rapid annealing will induce a bimodal grain structure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed processing will produce refined grains with a high density of deformation twins or nanotwins.
Fine grains and abundant twin boundaries will impede dislocation motion.
Twin-boundary migration and dynamic reorientation will provide additional deformation mechanisms that sustain strain hardening.
Sustained strain hardening from the proposed microstructure will improve uniform plastic deformation under dynamic loading.
The proposed microstructure will delay local strain localization under dynamic loading.
The processed alloy will have greater post-yield strain hardening and work absorption than the baseline alloy.
The processed alloy will have 20–30% greater uniform strain than the baseline under high-strain-rate loading.
The processed alloy will delay necking or shear-band formation relative to the baseline.
The processed alloy will absorb more impact energy than the baseline.
The processed alloy will exhibit a less abrupt impact-induced energy-release profile than the baseline.
The prediction applies to adiabatic dynamic or impact loading at strain rates above approximately 1000 s^-1.
The prediction may not apply at lower strain rates or when thermal dissipation is enhanced.
